card.summary: S. 1071, titled the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2026 and designated as Public Law No. 119-60, establishes the policies, authorizations, and funding levels for U.S. national defense programs, military construction, Department of Energy national security programs, intelligence activities, and maritime and Coast Guard operations. The legislation spans eight divisions covering defense acquisitions, authorizations for foreign affairs and intelligence, Coast Guard management and maritime safety reforms, security policies regarding foreign nations and illicit trafficking, and various other administrative matters.

card.summary: The Coast Guard Authorization Act of 2025 sets funding levels for the U.S. Coast Guard from fiscal year 2025 through 2029, authorizes military end-strength levels and training, creates a new civilian-led Office of the Secretary of the Coast Guard, and updates organizational authorities, acquisitions, personnel policies, vessel safety rules, and oil pollution response protocols.
card.title: Coast Guard Authorization Act of 2025

selection.reason: Impact scored and summarised by Gemini.

summary: The Coast Guard Authorization Act of 2025 authorizes appropriations for the U.S. Coast Guard for fiscal years 2025 and 2026, sets authorized levels of military strength and training, modifies acquisition and procurement rules, and establishes numerous policies and programs relating to Coast Guard personnel, the Coast Guard Academy, vessel safety, oil pollution response, and sexual assault and harassment prevention. Additionally, the legislation amends laws concerning merchant mariner credentials, the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration, and the South Pacific Tuna Treaty.

affected_groups.effect: Impacts active-duty members, reservists, civilians, and their dependents through updated pay, housing, family leave, behavioral health access, and travel allowances.
affected_groups.group: Coast Guard personnel and military families

affected_groups.effect: Alters licensing, credentialing standards, sea service requirements, training substitutions, and administrative procedures for commercial vessels.
Establishes new student advisory boards, room security enhancements with electronic locks, transfer options for victims of misconduct, and behavioral health wellness rooms.

key_provisions: Authorizes appropriations for Coast Guard operating expenses, acquisition, retired pay, and reserve training for fiscal years 2025 and 2026.
Updates personnel policies, including direct hire authorities, family leave expansions, behavioral health programs, travel allowances, and education initiatives.
Revises merchant mariner credentialing requirements, training substitutions, and electronic credentialing system standards under Title 46.
Expands policies and reporting requirements concerning sexual assault, sexual harassment, and other misconduct in the Coast Guard and at the Coast Guard Academy.
Establishes new requirements for vessel safety, security plans, cyber-incident training, and the regulation of uncrewed maritime systems.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The Coast Guard Authorization Act of 2025 authorizes appropriations for the U.S. Coast Guard for fiscal years 2025 and 2026, sets authorized levels of military strength and training, modifies acquisition and procurement rules, and establishes numerous policies and programs relating to Coast Guard personnel, the Coast Guard Academy, vessel safety, oil pollution response, and sexual assault and harassment prevention. Additionally, the legislation amends laws concerning merchant mariner credentials, the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration, and the South Pacific Tuna Treaty.
summary_detail.significance: The bill represents comprehensive, multi-year authorization legislation for the U.S. Coast Guard, impacting its organizational structure, capital acquisition projects, personnel management, and regulatory oversight of shipping, navigation, and environmental protection.
